newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends unchanged, gilt prices fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends unchanged, gilt prices fall.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday unchanged from the day's opening quotes on good liquidity while security prices fell in thin trade, dealers said.
Call money ended Tuesday in the 3.5-4.0 percent range, the band it had traded in throughout the day, they said.
"There was little movement in rates today," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Call was easy with a softish undertone as liquidity with the banking system is good."

Some dealers said they expected call money rates to firm up next week as companies make their advance tax payments ahead of a December 15 deadline. Analysts estimate the outflow to be between 40 and 50 billion rupees.
However other dealers said the market had already factored in the outflows and there would be little impact.
Prices of government securities fell slightly in thin trade, dealers said.
"There was not much buying interest today..this pushed prices down," said a dealer.

The 13.25 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded on Tuesday at 102.50 rupees against its last traded price of 102.70, dealers said. The 13.50 percent 1998 dropped to 102.50 rupees from 102.60 while the 13.62 percent 1998 fell to 103.55 rupees from 103.64, they said.
Dealers said the 364-day treasury bill maturing in December 1997 was traded at a yield of 10.17 percent against its last traded yield of 10.25 percent.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
